recent_posts.title: Helm Turns 10
recent_posts.summary: Helm, the Kubernetes package manager, celebrates its 10th anniversary. The project began during a hackathon in October 2015, shortly after Kubernetes 1.1.0 was released. The first commit was made on October 19, 2015, and Helm was showcased at the first KubeCon just weeks later. The original codebase, known as Helm v1, later merged with Deployment Manager and became part of the Kubernetes project, eventually growing into a thriving community of developers and charts.

recent_posts.title: Path To Releasing Helm v4
recent_posts.summary: Helm v4 has entered its alpha phase with the first alpha release available. The development follows a structured timeline: alpha period through September with feature freeze and API breaking changes, beta period in October focusing on stability, release candidates at end of October, and final release planned for KubeCon North America 2025 in mid-November. The community is encouraged to test and provide feedback during alpha, while SDK users should review API changes for compatibility.

recent_posts.title: Debian/Ubuntu Helm Apt Repository Move
recent_posts.summary: The Helm Apt repository for Debian and Ubuntu systems is migrating from Balto hosting to Buildkite. Users need to update their APT keys and repository references using the new installation instructions to continue receiving Helm updates through the package manager.

recent_posts.title: Helm @ KubeCon + CloudNativeCon EU '25
recent_posts.summary: Helm's team is attending KubeCon + CloudNativeCon EU 2025 in London from April 1-4. Key highlights include sessions on Helm 4 development, a Contribfest for engaging contributors, and a Helm booth in the Project Pavilion. Additionally, community-led sessions will address various cloud-native topics featuring Helm. Join Helm maintainers for talks and updates on the upcoming Helm 4 release.

recent_posts.title: Experience a Helm Release: Live at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America 2024!
recent_posts.summary: A live demonstration of the Helm release process will take place at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America 2024. Attendees can witness the steps involved in transforming source code into a consumable artifact for the cloud-native community. The session will be recorded and available later for those who cannot attend. This event is part of several Helm-related activities at the conference.

recent_posts.title: Helm at KubeCon/CloudNativeCon SLC
recent_posts.summary: Helm will be present at KubeCon/CloudNativeCon North America in Salt Lake City, with various activities throughout the main conference days. Key events include a live release, informational sessions on Helm v4, and opportunities to engage with maintainers and contribute to the project. Attendees can visit the project pavilion for in-person interactions and participate in sessions designed to introduce and discuss Helm 4.

recent_posts.title: Helm 2to3 is Now Unsupported
recent_posts.summary: Helm 2to3 tool is now officially unsupported, marking the end of security patches and updates. Users are strongly discouraged from using Helm 2to3 and are expected to have migrated to Helm 3. Helm 2 has been unsupported for over three years.

recent_posts.title: The Road to Helm 4
recent_posts.summary: Helm has established itself as the de-facto package manager for Kubernetes, widely used across various sectors. Adherence to backwards compatibility has limited the introduction of breaking changes but has still allowed for incremental feature updates. With Helm 3 introducing significant updates like post rendering and OCI registry support, Helm 4 is now in development, aiming to evolve the tool further. Community input at KubeCon EU 2024 has steered its direction towards support for additional templating languages, expanded plugin usage, and enhanced security measures. Opportunities for community involvement include roadmap meetings, Slack discussions, and GitHub contributions.

recent_posts.title: Response To CVE-2019-25210
recent_posts.summary: Response to CVE-2019-25210 filed against the Helm project. The project rejects the disclosure's assertion of a vulnerability. Changes have been made to provide greater clarity and hide secret information in the dry-run output of commands.

recent_posts.title: Helm 3.13
recent_posts.summary: Helm 3.13 brings significant changes and new features, including the ability for dry-run and template to connect to Kubernetes servers, improvements in values handling, the option to use JSON in the index.yaml file, and the introduction of the get metadata command.
